_doc: Generated code and its copies (graph.extract.common, graph.link). blocks: [begin, end] marker pairs inside a source file (graph.extract.common.mark_generated): a line that starts (after its indentation) with `begin` opens a block, the next line that starts with `end` closes it; every definition that lies inside is flagged generated (a verbatim copy that a generator writes into each file, so a member that the file does not use is not dead code: it is reported by nobody and edited by nobody). The shipped pairs are `// BEGIN GENERATED` .. `// END GENERATED` and `// <generated>` .. `// </generated>`; add the pair your generator writes. paths + path_exts: regexes of the repo-relative path of a SCHEMA file (its name ends with one of path_exts: .proto, .graphql, .sql, the schema languages of graph.extract.schema, never code of any other language: first-party code may live under vendored/ or google/cloud/) that is a vendored or generated copy (graph.link.path_flags, with its own table of vendor, node_modules, third_party, generated, *_pb2.py, *.pb.go for every language): such a file is not in the graph, so nobody is told that an object of it is unused; the protobuf well-known types and the googleapis protos that a project vendors are the case. headers: regexes searched in the first 1 KB of a schema file (graph.extract.schema): a file that says it is written by a generator is generated as a whole.
headers: Generated by the protocol buffer compiler
